# Tobit Chapter 1 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Disagreement 1 — TOB 1:2: Geographic Orientation of Thisbe

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "to the right of Kedesh of Naphtali" |
| LOGOS | "to the south of Kedesh-Naphtali" |
| PNEUMA | "on the southern edge of Kedesh-Naphtali" |

**Issue:** The Greek ek dexiōn literally means "from/to the right" but in ancient geographic convention (when oriented east) means "south." EMET preserves the literal spatial language; LOGOS and PNEUMA interpret geographically.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "to the south of Kedesh-Naphtali" (LOGOS). Standard ancient geographic orientation faced east; "right hand" = south. English readers need the directional meaning, not the literal body-orientation metaphor.

---

## Disagreement 2 — TOB 1:3: Opening Register and Self-Introduction

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "I, Tobit, walked in ways of truth and in righteous-deeds all the days of my life" |
| LOGOS | "I, Tobit, walked in the paths of truth and righteous deeds all the days of my life" |
| PNEUMA | "My name is Tobit, and all my life I tried to walk a straight path — doing what was right, showing kindness wherever I could" |

**Issue:** The formal autobiographical self-introduction (egō Tōbit) belongs to a Semitic narrative tradition. PNEUMA modernizes it into casual first-person narration, losing the genre marker.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. The "I, [Name]" construction is essential to the book's self-presentation as memoir/testimony. PNEUMA's paraphrase, while readable, drops the solemn register.

---

## Disagreement 3 — TOB 1:5: Identification of the Idol

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "to the heifer Baal" |
| LOGOS | "to the calf of Baal" |
| PNEUMA | "to the golden calf of Baal" |

**Issue:** The Greek damali tō Baal is grammatically "to the heifer, the Baal." EMET preserves female bovine (damalis = heifer); LOGOS uses "calf" (gender-neutral, more familiar OT term); PNEUMA adds "golden" with no textual basis.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "to Baal the calf." The noun is reordered so "Baal" functions as the proper name and "calf" as the appositional description. This matches the contemptuous OT naming pattern (cf. Hos 8:5-6, "your calf, O Samaria"). "Golden" is an embellishment not in the Sinaiticus text.

---

## Disagreement 4 — TOB 1:6: Frequency of Jerusalem Pilgrimages

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "I alone was-going-up often to Jerusalem in-the feasts" |
| LOGOS | "I alone would frequently go up to Jerusalem for the appointed feasts" |
| PNEUMA | "Every year, while everyone around me was offering sacrifices to false gods, I made the journey to Jerusalem alone" |

**Issue:** The Greek pollakis means "often/frequently," not "every year." PNEUMA introduces an annual frequency that is not in the text and is arguably inconsistent with Tobit's situation in the northern kingdom.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Frequently" accurately renders pollakis. PNEUMA's interpolation of contrast with idol-worshippers ("while everyone around me") and annual frequency both exceed the text.

---

## Disagreement 5 — TOB 1:7: Distribution of the Second Tithe

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "the second tithe in-silver I-was-redeeming six years [in a row] and was-going-up and was-spending [it] each year in Jerusalem" |
| LOGOS | "The second tithe I would convert to silver for six years and then go up to Jerusalem and spend it there each year" |
| PNEUMA | "For six years running I converted the second tithe into silver, traveled to Jerusalem, and spent it there each year as prescribed" |

**Issue:** The grammar of the six-year reckoning is ambiguous — does the six-year period precede spending, or does he convert and spend over six years? LOGOS and EMET imply a six-year saving then annual spending; PNEUMA implies annual conversion-and-spending across six years.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. The Greek structure places the six-year period with the converting, suggesting a saving cycle rather than annual trips. PNEUMA's "as prescribed" adds an unsupported qualifier.

---

## Disagreement 6 — TOB 1:8: Deborah's Relation to Tobit

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Deborah the-mother of Ananiel our-father" |
| LOGOS | "Deborah the mother of our forefather Ananiel" |
| PNEUMA | "my grandmother Deborah — Ananiel's mother" |

**Issue:** The Greek has "Ananiel our father" but PNEUMA translates "my grandmother." Strictly, Deborah is mother of Ananiel who is listed in the genealogy as Tobit's ancestor, making her great-grandmother or more distant. PNEUMA simplifies.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Our forefather Ananiel" is appropriately non-specific about generational distance. PNEUMA's "my grandmother" is an over-simplification of the genealogical chain.

---

## Disagreement 7 — TOB 1:13: Tobit's Role for Enemessar

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "his purchasing-agent" |
| LOGOS | "his purveyor" |
| PNEUMA | "the king's personal purchasing agent" |

**Issue:** The Greek agorastēs (one who buys in the agora/market) is a commercial functionary. LOGOS's "purveyor" is archaic English; EMET and PNEUMA agree on "purchasing agent"; PNEUMA adds "personal" and "the king's" for emphasis.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "his purchasing agent." EMET and PNEUMA align on the best modern equivalent. "Personal" is not in the Greek and is dropped.

---

## Disagreement 8 — TOB 1:14: Amount of Money Deposited

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "[money-bags of] silver, ten talents" |
| LOGOS | "ten talents of silver" |
| PNEUMA | "ten talents of silver" |

**Issue:** Minor only — EMET's bracketed "[money-bags of]" is an explanatory gloss not in the Greek; the Greek simply has "argyrion talanta deka."

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "ten talents of silver" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). EMET's gloss is unnecessary and slightly misleading; the talent is a unit of weight/currency, not necessarily bags.

---

## Disagreement 9 — TOB 1:18: The Divine Title in Judgment

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "the-King of Heaven executed upon him on-account-of the-blasphemies which he-had-blasphemed" |
| LOGOS | "the King of Heaven brought upon him for the blasphemies he had uttered" |
| PNEUMA | "that God brought on him for his arrogance and blasphemy" |

**Issue:** PNEUMA substitutes "God" for "King of Heaven" and adds "arrogance" (not in the Greek). The title "King of Heaven" (ho basileus tou ouranou) is a distinctive Tobit usage that should be preserved.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "King of Heaven" preserved. "Brought upon" is more natural than EMET's "executed upon." LOGOS's "the blasphemies he had uttered" is more natural than EMET's cognate "blasphemies which he had blasphemed."

---

## Disagreement 10 — TOB 1:21: How Sennacherib Was Killed

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "two of his sons killed him and they-fled to the mountains of Ararat" |
| LOGOS | "two of his sons murdered him and fled to the mountains of Ararat" |
| PNEUMA | "two of Sennacherib's own sons stabbed him in his sleep and fled" |

**Issue:** The Greek has apekteinan auton, "they killed him." PNEUMA adds "stabbed him in his sleep" — vivid historical embellishment not in the text.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Murdered" captures the intentional, treacherous nature of the act better than the neutral "killed." PNEUMA's details are an interpolation.

---

## Disagreement 11 — TOB 1:22: Achiacharus's Court Titles

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "chief-cup-bearer and keeper-of-the-ring and steward and accountant" |
| LOGOS | "chief cupbearer, keeper of the signet ring, steward, and treasurer" |
| PNEUMA | "chief cupbearer, keeper of the royal seal, steward, treasurer, second only to the king" |

**Issue:** The Greek oinochoos archōn = "chief cupbearer"; sphragistēs = "seal-keeper/signet-ring keeper"; oikonomos = "steward/administrator"; apodektēs = "treasurer/receiver." EMET's "accountant" for apodektēs is too narrow; LOGOS's "treasurer" is better. PNEUMA adds "second only to the king" which is actually in the text (deuteros) but both EMET and LOGOS address it separately.

**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Signet ring" is more precise than PNEUMA's "royal seal." The final note "Sarchedonus had made him second in authority" is handled in the following clause, as in LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements logged: 11**
